title: Mike LaFleur Press Conference: September 28, 2026
headline: LaFleur says Jeremiyah Love got a 'hot hand' and no injuries came out of the loss, but the offense still lacks explosive plays (longest run 8 yards) and Marvin Harrison Jr. is getting to his spots.
summary: LaFleur spent most of the session on the offense's lack of explosive plays through three weeks. The unit has stayed efficient for about 10 of 12 quarters, and the longest run against Seattle was only 8 yards. He blamed small details (footwork, busts, checkdowns that don't turn into YAC) and said the team won't abandon the under-center run game or the play-action concepts. He said penalties were the biggest drag, naming three early penalties that derailed the first three drives, and called the run-game problems busts that come down to coaching clarity. He called Jeremiyah Love's rhythm a 'hot hand' situation and said there is no set plan for how carries are distributed. He said Marvin Harrison Jr. responded well to the week's noise, getting to his spots and finding opportunities in the intermediate game. He praised linebacker Jack Gibbens as a great pickup and said no new injuries came out of the game. He said the defense needs more clarity on blitz timing, fronts and tackling. He also said the team is focused on itself rather than the Giants' quarterback situation (Jameis Winston), and that they travel east for a 10 a.m. body-clock kickoff.

injuries.detail: LaFleur said no one came out of the game with an injury beyond what was mentioned after the game: 'Nothing. All good there.'

signals.claim: Love can keep getting carries when he has the hot hand, with distribution decided week to week.
signals.note: Love seems to improve with volume, and the coach is open to feeding whoever is rolling, which is good for his workload.
signals.quote: it was kind of more the hot hand too

signals.claim: Harrison will keep getting to his spots in the intermediate passing game and the coaches will keep working with him.
signals.note: Coach pushed back on the noise around Harrison and sees his route work and targets in the intermediate game as encouraging.
signals.quote: he got to his spots. There were some opportunities in the intermediate

signals.claim: Gibbens will remain a key contributor in the defense.
signals.note: IDP managers get a positive signal: the coach calls him a great fit and says he's improving.
signals.quote: he's a stud.

signals.note: A deep shot to Wilson early in the game didn't connect because of a small breakdown, so shot plays to him are still being called.

topics.detail: Three weeks in, the offense has been efficient but not explosive. LaFleur wants to turn short completions into bigger gains with better YAC, blocking on the second and third levels, and ball placement, without forcing it.
The coach said penalties are on the team, not the opponent, and that three penalties on the first three drives killed the offense against a very good team.
Blitzes haven't worked because of small details in timing and fronts. Tackling needs to improve, and LaFleur blames coaches for not providing enough clarity.
LaFleur says the team will keep marrying the run with the pass and working under center, because that's what will make the offense good over the long run, while reevaluating each week.

The Giants just made a QB trade and haven't named a starter. LaFleur says the defensive plan won't change much, though they will study what Jameis Winston has done in situations like third down and the red zone.

title: Jesse Minter Discusses Big-Time Plays and Areas of Improvement From Week 3 Win
headline: Zay Flowers played 21 snaps in his return and is expected to move closer to full-time, while the Ravens' interior line is in flux after Gwyn and Pocic's long-term injuries.
summary: Minter praised the team's travel logistics and the 'come through when we needed to' finish in a close Week 3 win abroad, and said there is a lot to clean up in all three phases, especially penalties and missed tackles. Jovaughn Gwyn and Ethan Pocic both look long-term, with IR likely, so the line will be reshuffled. A first-round rookie was rolled in at center mid-game and handled the protection duties, and the staff may add a piece or two this week. Carson Vinson started at left tackle for Ronnie Stanley (toe) and held up well, with Stanley expected to be closer to returning this week. Nnamdi Madubuike played a full workload in his first game back in over a year and showed pass-rush ability. Zay Flowers was held to about 21 snaps and Minter expects him to push toward near full-time work. Travis Jones' minor injury is nothing to worry about. Minter took responsibility for the defense's inconsistency and tackling, and defended the aggressive fourth-and-short and goal-line calls even though they failed. Special teams were a bright spot, and Lamar Jackson's leadership and OC Declan Doyle's late play call were praised.

injuries.detail: Minter said both he and Ethan look long-term and are likely headed to IR, with a decision in the next couple of days.
Described as a longer-term injury along with Gwyn, with IR anticipated. Minter said the team will figure it out over the next few days.
Dealing with a toe issue. Minter expects him to be a lot closer this week to pushing back into the lineup.
Played 21 snaps after a concern about his health and the field. Minter wants to build him toward closer to full-time work.
Minor in-game injury; Minter said he is fine.
Played in his first game in more than a year and held up well.

signals.claim: Flowers' snap count will increase from 21 toward near full-time work in coming weeks.
signals.note: Workload was deliberately capped in his return, so his snaps and target opportunities should rise.
signals.quote: we wanted to keep it in the 20 to 25 snap range.

signals.claim: Stanley will be closer to returning to the left tackle job this week.
signals.note: His toe health decides whether Vinson keeps starting, which affects Lamar Jackson's protection and the run game.
signals.quote: be a lot closer this week to being able to, to push back

signals.claim: Vinson played well as the starting left tackle and gave up no sacks.
signals.note: He is a solid fill-in, but his job is likely to end if Stanley is healthy.
signals.quote: I thought he played really well.

signals.claim: The first-round rookie, who moved to center mid-game, will prepare to potentially play center again this week, with the best five linemen still to be determined.
signals.note: Interior line instability after the Gwyn and Pocic injuries could affect offensive efficiency and the run game.
signals.quote: he was up to speed enough to be able to do everything

signals.claim: Madubuike will keep a full role and improve as he gets further from his long layoff.
signals.note: He is back as an interior pass rusher, which helps the defense's pressure and sack potential.
signals.quote: he'll get better and better and better as we go

signals.note: Minter praised his plays late in the game after a penalty, which suggests his role is secure.

topics.detail: Minter said penalties on offense hurt at key moments and the defense is still chasing consistency and getting everyone on the same page. He put the responsibility on himself.
He called the missed tackles a detail problem involving angles, body position and diving for big hits. He cited a tight end checkdown that turned into an explosive play.

Minter liked the decisions to go for it on fourth and short and at the goal line, but said the blocking failed and an inside backer ran through. He said they need more volume of plays ready inside the five.

Minter was very happy with special teams: conservative kickoffs, a punt return that set up the go-ahead drive, the punter playing through illness, and Keondre Jackson blocking a field goal. The game-winning kick was a long one.
Lamar Jackson gave a Saturday night speech, and Minter called him the 'make it work' player. He credited Declan Doyle and the practiced situational script for the final play call.
The Ravens return home for a normal week, with Minter stressing a one-game-season mindset and focusing on cleaning up self-inflicted errors.

title: Jesse Minter Recaps Ravens' Thrilling Win Over Cowboys
headline: Ravens beat Dallas 34-31 on a last-second Lamar Jackson to Zay Flowers play; Gwynn and Ioane's OL situation is unresolved, with no injury updates given.
summary: Minter opened by thanking everyone involved in the Brazil trip and crediting Dallas as a good team, calling the win a baby step. He was critical of the defense over the final quarter but praised the goal-line stand that held Dallas to a field goal from first-and-goal at the one. The game ended on a play with seven seconds left, after Dallas kicked a touchback: Lamar Jackson and Zay Flowers hit a big gain to get the team into range, and the kicker (apparently Tyler Loop, transcribed as 'Luke') then won it. Minter said the team missed chances to extend leads, including aggressive fourth-down calls where he valued touchdowns over field goals. He praised the kicker's process and mindset after the early-season struggles. In the injury discussion, he said there were no updates on Gwynn and another lineman, and noted Ioane stepped in at a key moment and executed late after the team had been repping him there. He also praised Roquan Smith as the defensive leader who wears the green dot, and pointed to a first-half sack as a big play. He closed by saying the team will focus on recovering from the ten-hour flight and taking it one week at a time.

injuries.detail: Left the game and Minter said there is no update; the team will have to wait and see.

signals.claim: Ioane will continue to be the next man up on the interior offensive line if Gwynn or another lineman is unavailable.
signals.note: Ioane played in a key late moment without mistakes, so he could start or see snaps if the interior OL injuries linger, which affects the Ravens' run game and pass protection.

signals.claim: Gwyn's availability for next week will be determined after evaluation.
signals.note: His absence would weaken the interior line and affect the offense's efficiency.
signals.quote: no updates on those guys. We'll have to wait and see

signals.claim: Flowers is a go-to target in key situations, including the end-of-game play practiced for the seven-second scenario.
signals.note: Trusted by Lamar in the clutch, which supports his WR1 role and target share.
signals.quote: Unbelievable play by Lamar and Zay

signals.claim: Roquan Smith remains the defensive leader and green-dot play-caller.
signals.note: Strong IDP signal for a secure every-down role.
signals.quote: He wears the green dot. He gets everybody going.

topics.detail: Minter said the final play worked because of the seven seconds left and the touchback rule, which put the ball at the 35 and required about 18 yards to reach range. The team prepares for these situations.
The defense held Dallas to a field goal after first-and-goal at the one, but Minter was not satisfied with the last quarter and wanted one or two more red-zone stops.
The team chose aggressive fourth downs because touchdowns are more valuable than field goals, and missed some chances to extend leads.
The ten-hour flight each way in Brazil requires recovery time, and Minter said the field held up well and did not bother the team.
Minter defended the kicker through early struggles, citing his training camp performance, his process, and his positive mindset.

title: Joe Brady Reflects On Bills Win And Performance Against The Chargers
headline: Ty Johnson is back and impactful, but Brady says he must get Ray Davis more snaps; Christian Benford's status is unresolved, and Keon Coleman and Greg Rousseau drew praise.
summary: Brady said injury updates will come as players recover from the game. He is not worried about Josh Allen's usual day-after soreness, and he gave no firm update on Christian Benford, who left the game hurt. He praised the outside corners behind Benford, Maxwell Hairston and Davison Igbinosun, and said he is confident in whoever is on the field. He took blame for the turnovers, citing a poor play call, and stressed ball security and fighting for extra yards (he praised Dalton Kincaid's run after catch). He felt the defense improved on third down and against the run, and he credited better communication now that the group is healthier. He called the QB sneak and goal-line packages complicated, said they will keep evolving, and defended his aggressive fourth-down calls. He said Ty Johnson, back after missing the preseason and game reps, brings a unique dynamic. He also said he needs to get Ray Davis more playing time because Davis has earned it. He called Keon Coleman outstanding, saying he made plays beyond the big one, and credited Bradley Chubb's veteran leadership for Greg Rousseau's confident start. He noted the OLB rotation shrank because of how the game went, but said more reps are coming for players who have earned them.

injuries.detail: Left the game injured; Brady gave no diagnosis and said they will see how players progress over the next couple of days.
Got banged up in the game, but Brady said he is usually sore the day after and he is not concerned.
Brady said he and Keon Coleman were not able to get reps in practice, and the team is still figuring out whether they can play.

signals.note: Brady explicitly said Davis needs more playing time, which raises his flex and handcuff value alongside Ty Johnson.
signals.quote: Now I got to get Ray playing more right.

signals.claim: Ty Johnson will keep a meaningful role now that he is back from injury, while his snaps are managed alongside Ray Davis.
signals.note: He is back after missing the preseason and made key plays; his role is likely to be shared with Davis.
signals.quote: when he's on the field somehow the ball finds him and good things happen.

signals.note: Brady praised him as outstanding and said he made plays beyond the big one, which supports his WR value.
signals.quote: Kim was outstanding yesterday.

signals.claim: Rousseau will continue to get pass-rush opportunities, with more reps coming for earned players.
signals.note: For IDP, his confident start (two sacks in the game, six on the season) keeps him a top edge option, though Brady warned against complacency.
signals.quote: Greg is in a position right now where he's, he's playing confidently.

signals.claim: Kincaid will keep being used after the catch, with an emphasis on ball security.
signals.note: Brady praised his run after catch but raised fumble concerns, which are a mild risk.
signals.quote: Dalton Kincaid was outstanding, you know, outstanding run after catch.

signals.note: Unusual sneak packages could change goal-line and short-yardage usage, but Brady called it a work in progress.

signals.claim: Hairston will keep playing outside corner, including more if Benford misses time.
signals.note: IDP and defense-streamer relevant: he is a key outside corner if Benford is out.
signals.quote: I thought Max played well yesterday.

signals.claim: Igbinosun will keep playing outside corner and gain reps, especially if Benford misses time.
signals.note: Brady said he is confident and made big plays and good run fits.
signals.quote: he's confident, um, you know, he made that had some big plays

signals.claim: Benford's availability will be determined over the next couple of days.
signals.note: His status matters for the Bills' secondary and IDP value.
signals.quote: We'll kind of see how they kind of progress these next couple days.

topics.detail: Brady took responsibility for the turnovers, citing a poor play call and the need to be on the same page with Allen on decisions. He wants more intentionality going to the ground and covering the ball.

He felt the defense played well on third down and against the run, improved its communication, and was helped by a big interception early on. He wants to clean up third-and-long and open-field tackling.
Brady said he was decisive on the fourth-and-six and third/fourth-and-one calls and will stay aggressive, using two-possession thinking.
He said the packages involve many alerts and checks and will keep evolving, and he declined to give details.

title: Dave Canales provides injury updates after Browns game
headline: Jaycee Horn likely headed to IR with a significant quad injury, while Jalen Coker (quad), Michael Jackson (groin), Damien Lewis (elbow) and Bryce Young (sore ankle) are all being evaluated. Young is expected to play vs. the Lions.
summary: Canales said Jaycee Horn has a significant quad injury, that the team is gathering second and third opinions, and that IR looks likely, with full details coming Wednesday. Michael Jackson also hurt his groin and is still being evaluated, so cornerback depth is thin. Will Lee, Akayleb Evans and Chau Smith-Wade are in the mix, and Corey Thornton could be elevated from the practice squad. Jalen Coker strained his quad, Damien Lewis has an elbow issue, and both are getting imaging. Canales noted a coming bye week and said the team is weighing Coker's availability against his long-term health. Devin Lloyd is expected back this week, Xavier Legette is day to day with a knee issue, and Nick Scott's rib issue looks playable. Bryce Young was sore after taking a cleat to the ankle, will get further evaluation including imaging, and is expected to play Sunday night against the Lions. Canales said Browns corner Denzel Ward shadowed Tetairoa McMillan (2 catches, 17 yards on 5 targets), that the staff must move him around more, and that they will get him more involved. He praised the use of Darren Waller, Brycen Tremayne and John Metchie, and said the tight end room is coming to life. He also credited Chuba Hubbard's downhill running in the second half.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference: September 28th, 2026
headline: Browns are on a short week for Thursday at Pittsburgh. Tyson Campbell was close to playing and Monken feels good about him. Tytus Howard's false starts are a concern, Denzel Boston needs more targets, and the Watson-led passing game is still 'under construction'.
summary: Monken said he hadn't watched the tape because the team moved straight to Pittsburgh for a Thursday game. He called the Watson-and-receivers connection a work in progress and said the offense is 'under construction'. Watson showed no lingering effects from a fourth-quarter hit. The offensive line penalties, including cadence and false-start issues, were called embarrassing at home and must be fixed quickly. He also admitted short-yardage failures come from scheme, communication and losing at the point of attack. Monken said the Browns can do a better job of moving Denzel Boston around and targeting him, but he doesn't control where the ball goes, and he blamed protection, game flow and poor throwing for the low wide receiver volume. On defense he praised Denzel Ward and Grant Delpit for playing up to their extensions, and said Quincy Williams looked much faster and more comfortable. Tyson Campbell was close to playing and Monken feels good about him for Thursday. A teammate's knee injury (the name was garbled in captions) had no update yet, and Monken expected more information later in the day.

signals.note: He returned to play and looks healthy going into the short week.

topics.detail: Monken called the penalties embarrassing at home and said they must be fixed quickly. He listed shifts and motions, alignment, and snap-count discipline as causes, with Watson also responsible for owning the line of scrimmage.

The team moved on to Pittsburgh right after the game. Monken said the day after the game is like a Wednesday/Thursday of a normal week, and injury clarity will come over the next couple of days.

title: HC Sean Payton on Broncos’ win over Rams: ‘Really, a tale of two halves’
headline: Broncos beat the Rams 30-26 after a poor first half. Payton wants the offense to start faster and run more under center, and Marvin Mims Jr. is still out as a returner.
summary: Payton called the win gutsy and a tale of two halves. The defense struggled early, while the offense improved after halftime thanks to a better run balance, big plays and opportunistic penalties. He said the runs kept the offense on schedule and took pressure off the QB, and he stressed under-center football. Talanoa Hufanga got the game ball for his pick-six and a play at the end of the game, and Payton praised him as a consistent performer and leader. He was candid that the slow starts, in Week 1 and again in this game, are a real concern. He said Bo Nix is not the problem, because the issue starts with the coaches and the group, and it will cost them in bigger games if it isn't fixed. He explained that he went for two in the third quarter because the game was low-scoring (16-6) and he liked the plays they had. A young returner, likely Kolbe Katsis, got his first chance and Payton called it a good first night. Payton said he hopes to get Marvin Mims Jr. back soon.

injuries.detail: Payton said he hopes to get Mims back soon, which suggests he is currently unavailable, probably as a returner. No specifics on the injury or timeline.

signals.note: Payton praised Hufanga as a consistent leader after a pick-six and a late play, which is good for his IDP value.
signals.quote: I love him. I love coaching him.

signals.claim: Denver will try to start games faster and use more under-center and run-game balance to take pressure off Nix.
signals.note: Nix has had slow starts in two games, and the offense is leaning on the run and under-center work to settle him in. Early-game production is a risk.
signals.quote: we have to find a way to play better earlier

signals.note: The young returner made his debut with a 28-yard return that set up a touchdown. He may keep a return role while Mims is out, which matters only for special-teams value.
signals.quote: I think it was a good first night.

signals.claim: Mims is expected to return soon, though no timeline was given.
signals.note: His return-game and WR depth role is on hold until he is back.
signals.quote: hopefully we can get Marvin back here soon

topics.detail: Payton said the second-half runs kept Denver on schedule and took pressure off the QB. He also stressed the importance of under-center football. He said he didn't give his play-caller any mandates.
Denver has had low-scoring first halves in Week 1 and again in this game. Payton said he can't be comfortable with that, and that it will cost them in bigger games if it isn't fixed.
Payton went for two in the third quarter at 16-6 because the game was low-scoring and he loved the plays. He said he would have just kicked the extra point if the score had been higher.
A penalty forced a rekick and left Denver near its own 23-yard line, and Payton was unhappy with the new kickoff rule's effect. A short punt bailed them out.

title: HC Sean Payton on WR Pat Bryant vs. Rams: ‘It’s good to see him come up [big] in a game like that’
headline: Sean Payton praised WR Pat Bryant's hands, contested catches, and run-after-catch ability after his Week 3 game vs. the Rams, a positive usage signal.
summary: Payton said he was glad to see Pat Bryant produce in a game like the Rams win, noting Bryant has strong hands away from his body and high-pointed the two-point conversion target. He credited quarterback Bo Nix for finding a throwing lane, and said Bryant's run-after-catch skill, which the staff saw throughout training camp, showed up in live action. On penalties, Payton said the season is long, he has not seen a call reversed, and his focus is on penalties the team controls, such as pre-snap and post-snap ones. He downplayed the importance of the gun-versus-under-center split so far, noting only about three short-yardage snaps this season, and said the team typically lines up under center in short yardage when it plans to run. On the slow start, he said he did not think urgency was the main issue, pointing to defensive success and a tale-of-two-halves game, and said the fix is cleaning up early-down efficiency and the details of the game plan. He said the Rams' heavy passing late was mostly a byproduct of trailing in the second half, not a planned approach. He also said Bryant's movement on the two-point play was natural rather than something the team practices.

signals.claim: Bryant showed well in the Rams game, with the coach highlighting his hands, contested catch, and yards after catch.
signals.note: Payton's public praise, along with a two-point conversion target, suggests Bryant's role in the passing game is real and worth monitoring for volume.
signals.quote: it's good to see him, um, come up in a game like that.

topics.detail: Payton said he has not seen a penalty reversed and prefers to focus on penalties the team can control, such as pre-snap and post-snap ones.
Payton said the sample of gun snaps in short yardage is too small to judge, since the team has only about three such snaps so far, and it is usually under center when it plans to run.
Payton disputed that a lack of urgency caused the slow start. He pointed to strong defensive play and said the fix is early-down efficiency and game-plan details.
Payton said Stafford's high attempt total came mainly from the Rams trailing late, not from a planned pass-heavy approach.

title: Campbell on individual performances
headline: Lions' offense was efficient, not explosive: Goff 78% completions, Gibbs a game-ball winner, and Amon-Ra St. Brown had a minor, non-serious ailment. CB Ennis Rakestraw earns more outside reps and Cade Mays is unlikely for Carolina.
summary: Campbell called the Week 3 win over the Jets a good bounce-back after the Buffalo loss. He handed out game balls to Gibbs, Goff, Chuck Clark, Hutchinson and Jacob Saylors, and praised the offensive line (Mahogany, Scruggs, Miller, Ratledge) for setting the tone. Offensively the Lions were highly efficient, with Goff completing 78%, no turnovers, and 117 rushing yards at 4.7 per carry. They had few explosive plays because the Jets played a lot of shell coverage, and Goff took the underneath throws instead of forcing the ball. Campbell was frustrated that the first two drives produced no points and that a fourth-down failure was caused by an illegal formation. Defensively the Lions started fast, stopped the run, and got sacks, hits and a late takeaway, though they lost too many one-on-ones and took some costly penalties. Rakestraw will see more outside corner reps, Trevor Nowaske earned a bigger role, and Hutchinson drew heavy attention that helped Alim McNeill. Cade Mays is unlikely to play this week, and Thomas Harper is out for a while with no clear return. St. Brown had a minor issue and Campbell expects him to be fine.

title: Klint Kubiak on the resilience shown in Raiders’ Week 3 come-from-behind victory
headline: Mike Washington Jr. has 'earned more opportunities' after a big run, Jack Bech is out for a bit, and Jeanty and Powers-Johnson are expected back this week.
summary: Kubiak opened by saying Jack Bech will be out for a little while and that no roster decision (such as an IR move) has been made. He said Bech took a hit to the forearm and that the team was lucky it wasn't a concussion. Jackson Powers-Johnson has a sore groin and is still being evaluated, but Kubiak expects him back this week. Ashton Jeanty was taped at both ankles during the game. Kubiak said everyone is sore and he anticipates Jeanty back at some point this week. Rookie RB Mike Washington Jr. made a big impact, and Kubiak said he has earned more opportunities. He praised Nakobe Dean as a leader and credited the four fourth-quarter turnovers for the comeback win. He said Cody White and Dareke Young have surpassed expectations in the passing game and on special teams. Michael Mayer, newly extended, was singled out for a big goal-line play even with Brock Bowers back. Kubiak admitted the run game against the Saints needs to keep improving, and the team now turns to the undefeated Chiefs at home.

The Chiefs are also undefeated and come to Las Vegas next. Kubiak said that being a division game raises the stakes, and the team is starting from scratch.

title: HC Jeff Hafley - Sept 27 | Postgame Press Conference
headline: De'Von Achane left with a knee injury that Hafley said 'does not sound very optimistic'. Ollie Gordon and Malik Washington are the backfield names to watch while an update is pending.
summary: Hafley said the Dolphins are still gathering information on Achane's knee and hope to have more on Monday, but the early read is not optimistic. He declined to discuss how the offense would adjust without Achane until the severity is known. He praised the team's resilience in the 24-10 loss to the Chiefs. The game was close into the third quarter, the defense settled down after an early big play, and the offensive line improved. Ollie Gordon had a nice game with some big runs, and Malik Washington filled in as the emergency running back, which Hafley said the team had confidence in. Hafley said QB Malik Willis made big throws and runs and is improving in his first year as a true starter. He liked how corner Chris Bell responded to a penalty, and he praised rookie LB Jacob Rodriguez for his interception and his progress. On the Chop Robinson roughing-the-passer call, he hadn't seen the play and said he won't fault a player for going hard. He also said the defense improved over the previous week but still needs to be better.

title: Kevin O'Connell Talks About The Trade of J.J. McCarthy, Justin Jefferson's Ankle, Win Over Tampa Bay
headline: Justin Jefferson has only an ankle sprain (no long-term issue) and is day-to-day, while Josh Oliver is out for surgery with a torn bicep, leaving T.J. Hockenson and the tight end group to absorb more work.
summary: O'Connell opened by addressing the trade of J.J. McCarthy to the Giants, calling it an emotional day and stressing his respect for McCarthy and the relationship, while backing the front office's decision. He said he is confident in the remaining quarterback room of Kyler Murray, Carson Wentz and Max Bredeson. He acknowledged the offense still needs to mesh and improve, said he needs to coach better, and noted the team is 3-0 with a home game coming at U.S. Bank Stadium. On injuries, Josh Oliver has a torn bicep requiring surgery, and the tight end group as a whole, not just T.J. Hockenson, will need to fill the void. Justin Jefferson has an ankle sprain that avoided anything long term, and his week will be about reducing swelling and seeing what kind of work week he can have. A player he called Chuck Demmings (not on the roster) has a hamstring strain and will likely miss some time. Most of the rest of the session was reflection on McCarthy's development, the draft evaluation, and the summer quarterback competition, which he said he does not regret. He said Murray played only 11 snaps in one game and that the offense's issues go beyond the quarterback, citing correctable pre- and post-snap issues on tape.

title: Head Coach Mike Vrabel 9/28: "The answers are here, they are in this building"
headline: Vrabel says Drake Maye has no known shoulder issue after a rough loss at Jacksonville; interior line is unsettled with Greg Van Roten undergoing more tests and Ben Brown returning from injury.
summary: Vrabel took a lot of the blame after a lopsided road loss to Jacksonville, saying the answers are in the building and the team has to get back to basics and build its identity. He said he is unaware of any lingering shoulder problem for Drake Maye, with nothing that would have put him on the injury report, and he does not expect it to be an issue going forward. He used a golf-club analogy to say Maye, like the team, is pressing and that confidence has to come from preparation and practice reps, not from being told to be confident. On the offensive line, he said Ben Brown was the planned center and first left guard in, that it's good to have him back healthy, and that he will likely be needed to help this week. Walter Rouse got the start and made some mistakes but competed. Greg Van Roten's status will be determined after a few more tests. Vrabel said the protection continued to improve and credited the red-zone failures, turnovers and a missed field goal for the game getting away from them. He said the defense was poor in the red zone (Jacksonville went 5-for-5) and that this must be fixed. He doesn't expect big practice changes this week, though he is considering simplifying and doing less better. He also acknowledged a timeout after the second offensive play and said the offense needs to be more decisive.

title: Kellen Moore recaps Saints' loss to Raiders in Week 3 9/28/2026

He liked the run game, which went 28 for 148, though Tyler Shough's long scramble inflated the total. He credited better physicality, more movement up front and a deeper point of contact. He praised Noah Fant's run blocking and said the red zone and third-down offense (60% on third down) keep trending up. Travis Etienne will lose time with a hamstring injury and Moore would not say whether IR is coming. Anfernee Jennings and Pete Werner also left the game, and the team will gather more information. Moore said ball security needs to improve in every phase of the offense. He also covered Brock Bowers' big day, a penalty on Danny Stutsman and the "mysterious calls" questions, and said he is open to using a sixth offensive lineman. He framed the 1-2 start as a roller coaster the team has to ride out ahead of the Falcons game.

title: Coach John Harbaugh on J.J. McCarthy trade, Brian Burns injury
headline: Giants traded for J.J. McCarthy after Jackson (Dart) got hurt, but Jameis Winston remains the starter; Brian Burns (ACL) is done, so Kayvon Thibodeaux and Abdul Carter absorb more pass-rush snaps.
summary: Harbaugh said the Giants acquired J.J. McCarthy that morning after weeks of searching for quarterback help following Jackson's injury, calling him talented and a strong young QB. He insisted Jameis Winston is the starter against the Cardinals on Sunday and "for as long as I can see into the future," while saying McCarthy will be either the No. 2 or No. 3 QB this week and the backup job (McCarthy or Jake) is undecided. McCarthy faces a crash course in the offense, with extra work and a game-by-game approach; the coaching staff sees some overlap with the Minnesota system. Brian Burns tore his ACL and will have surgery, which Harbaugh called a big loss and a leadership blow to the defense. Abdul Carter and Kayvon Thibodeaux are expected to take on bigger roles, though both already play heavy snaps. Harbaugh said the run defense has been solid but the pass rush needs to improve, as opponents are using quick throws and chips to blunt it. He did not rule out a free-agent QB workout, saying all options are on the table.

title: HC Aaron Glenn Press Conference (9/28) | Week 4
headline: Breece Hall's injury is unclear, and Glenn pointed to Braelon Allen and Isaiah Davis as the backups. Garrett Wilson cleared the head injury, and Geno Smith got strong praise after going 31 of 37.
summary: Glenn said he will give a fuller injury update Wednesday, with Breece Hall and Dylan Parham the two he will focus on. Garrett Wilson was cleared from his head injury and won't be an issue. Glenn said he is concerned about Hall but doesn't know the extent of the injury yet, and he pointed to Braelon Allen and Isaiah Davis as the options behind him. He admitted the run game hasn't been good enough the last two weeks and said fixing it is an urgent priority, even though the passing game has developed well. He praised Geno Smith for delivering the ball with confidence under heavy pressure and for going 31 of 37, including to the tight ends and Wilson. He blamed the untouched blitz on an O-line miscommunication plus Geno needing to hold onto the ball. Minkah Fitzpatrick and another player who missed the game have no firm timeline, and Glenn will lean on the medical staff. He also said D'Angelo Ponds is improving each week but has to earn more playing time, and that his nickel and outside corner packages didn't get much run. The next opponent is Chicago.

headline: Jalen Warren (shoulder) was the workhorse in a 30-27 win and is the lead back for a short-week Thursday trip to Cleveland; Jalen Ramsey's wrist is a question and Rico Dowdle's status is still unclear.
summary: McCarthy praised Jalen Warren, who earned the offensive game ball, and said his yards after contact keep impressing him. He explained that snap and carry splits are planned in a Friday play-time meeting with the coordinators, but the game flow (expecting to score) pushed Warren's workload higher than planned. He was complimentary of rookie right tackle Max Iheanachor, who played next to Brock Hoffman, saying he showed no hesitancy, had no pre-snap problems apart from one penalty, and that Hoffman is the best veteran a young lineman could be paired with. McCarthy said he hopes Joey Porter gets more work this week and that there is a plan for him, but gave no firm timeline. He said Jalen Ramsey has a wrist injury and it is too early to tell his availability, though he expects Ramsey to try to play. McCarthy attributed Dylan Everette's snaps to Dylan pushing for playing time, not to any criticism of Asante Samuel Jr. He also praised Darnell Washington as a natural pass catcher and a key part of the program. title: Head Coach Mike Macdonald Recaps Sunday's Loss, Looks Ahead To Week 4
headline: Julian Love is day-to-day and Zach Charbonnet's practice return is still undecided, with an answer expected Monday. Jadarian Price keeps the backfield trust after his fumble, and Trevon Diggs is close to playable.
summary: Macdonald called his reaction to the Week 3 loss to Washington "mixed emotions": good flashes in all three phases, but a sense of urgency because the team isn't there yet. He gave Washington credit for the run-game struggles and said the offense found better answers in the second half, when being down multiple scores forced it to throw. He said Jadarian Price understands he must protect the ball, and the team will keep giving him carries. Julian Love is day-to-day after extensive work Sunday morning. Zach Charbonnet has no update, and a decision on whether he starts practicing this week should come by Monday. Trevon Diggs is practicing well and is part of the conversation to play soon. Macdonald praised Nick Emmanwori's game and said the staff is working out how to use him across three position groups. He said Jaxon Smith-Njigba had his best blocking game in a while, though the ball will find other receivers eventually. He called special teams "not good enough" after some big kick returns, and he reflected warmly on his year under Jim Harbaugh at Michigan ahead of facing him.

He was proud of the defense's effort and physicality. He said the unit took many shots at the ball without forcing turnovers and could have taken better advantage of some situations.

Macdonald said the team's special teams consistency through three weeks is not good enough after several sizable kick returns. He said a Seahawk play needs to look like a Seahawk play, and everyone is eligible for special teams.
The staff holds a weekly process meeting around noon and tweaks routines rather than making wholesale changes. He said he would overhaul things if needed.
Macdonald said his one year on Harbaugh's Michigan staff was foundational. Harbaugh gave him autonomy and belief, and the year shaped the team's "12 is one" vision.

title: Todd Bowles on Being Fundamentally Sound | Press Conference
headline: Baker Mayfield is out a minimum of three weeks with a dislocation, so undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels takes over a 0-3 offense that is struggling with penalties and sacks.
summary: Bowles said Mayfield's injury is consistent with a dislocation, with no ligament or tendon damage. He will miss at least three weeks, possibly less, and Tampa Bay is not yet committing to IR. Rookie Jalon Daniels will step in, and the team will look at a veteran or practice-squad quarterback for depth. Bowles expects defenses to blitz Daniels heavily and show him many looks. Jalen McMillan's MRI was still underway, so there was no update. Bucky Irving is not on the injury report despite questions about his late-game absence. Bowles blamed the offensive struggles on six offensive holding penalties, a chop penalty and six sacks. Those came from holding the ball too long, blocking breakdowns and coaching. He said he was not sure the offense has an identity yet but that it needs one quickly. He praised SirVocea Dennis and Christian Rozeboom for filling in for Josiah Trotter. Trotter and Rueben Bain are "too early" to call for this week, and a kick return touchdown came from a bad coverage alignment.

title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Jackson Slater (foot) and Fernando Carmona are both being evaluated. Saleh stood behind Cam Ward after the final-play mistake, praised Jeffery Simmons, and said Gunnar Helm could grow into a red-zone threat but has to earn it.
summary: Saleh opened with injuries. Carmona is still being evaluated, and Slater finished the game but carries a pretty significant foot injury, with more known as the week goes on. He called the offense's first-half efficiency poor in all three games, blaming drops on third down and critical situations plus a lack of precision. He said Cam Ward could deliver better balls at times. He defended Ward's decision making, calling the last-play throw a bad decision but not a reckless one, and said the offensive line protected well. He said the second half was elite by EPA and efficiency, but the offense got inside the red zone three times for only seven points. Saleh said he wished he had taken the field goal on the fourth-and-five decision, though he explained his reasoning about limited possessions. He raved about Jeffery Simmons, who had ten tackles and a sack, saying he has never seen a defensive tackle do that. He expressed full faith in the return man, who has fumbled twice in three games, and said Gunnar Helm is improving every week and could become more of a red-zone option, but has to earn it.
